text:
monitoring-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx and high p95 latency observed for Hosted API and several Dedicated pools in ap-south-2 starting ~2026-03-15T12:34Z. Error signature: STS 403/429 + CloudWatch Logs PutLogEvents failures. Impacting token exchange and observability ingestion, correlates with request spike from regional customers. Auto-runbooks triggered.

lee (oncall): I'm on it, grabbing pager. Switching to incident channel.

pagerduty: Pager duty triggered for rotation: lee -> nora.

nora (sre): joining. quick check: routing metrics show 18% 5xx for Hosted API in ap-south-2 over last 10m, Dedicated pool az-a and az-b seeing 12-15% 5xx. Latency p95 climbed from 120ms -> 850ms.

samir (infra): observability shows CloudWatch Logs ingestion errors: "PutLogEvents failed: ThrottlingException" across multiple shards. AWS STS calls are returning 429/500 intermittently when assuming roles for Dedicated hosts.

kate (product): any customer-facing impact? Frank pls coordinate CS.

frank (cs): already getting a few inbound support tickets. Notifying top 3 affected accounts with preliminary note.

lee (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable non-critical logging export to CloudWatch from inference workers in ap-south-2 (to reduce CW ingress). 2) Flip smart-routing policy to prefer ap-south-1 for new Hosted API requests for region-tagged traffic. 3) For Dedicated customers in ap-south-2, enable cross-region fallback to us-east-1 reserved pools. 4) Throttle internal background batch jobs.

ops-bot: Runbook step executed: disabled debug log export on 24 hosts in pool-a (command: fleetctl run --role inference --cmd 'service exporter stop' --filter pool=ap-south-2).

nora (sre): quick checks: health endpoints on inference nodes still OK, KV cache healthy. Problem is AWS role STS calls failing during credential refresh causing auth 5xx from our auth proxy. If we reduce reliance on STS for short-lived refresh we can reduce immediate errors.

samir (infra): temporary workaround: switch some hosts to use long-lived instance profile tokens (renew every 6h) instead of per-request STS assume-role. Implementing on a small canary of 6 hosts now.

lee (oncall): canary rolling now. paste logs:
```
[12:41:10] auth-proxy error: assume-role failed status=429 body="Rate exceeded"
[12:41:12] cw-logs exporter error: PutLogEvents ThrottlingException: Rate exceeded
[12:41:18] request-proxy 503 making call to model runtime: upstream: auth failure
```

nora (sre): opening AWS support case and checking for public region notices.

aws-support-bot: AWS Health: No open region-wide outage for ap-south-2. Creating Case ID: 1234567890 - "STS/CloudWatch throttling observed from customer side".

lee (oncall): I've pushed routing override: new requests from ap-south-2 with soft affinity now preferentially route to ap-south-1. Old sessions still try ap-south-2. Monitoring error rate for ap-south-2 after override.

samir (infra): rolling long-lived profile to 6 -> 18 -> 50 hosts. watching auth errors. so far on canary 0 STS 429s in 6m, 5xx rate down to 6% in those hosts.

nora (sre): action items for mitigation logged in incident tracker: reduce CW exports, enable longer-lived creds, route traffic, throttle background batches.

kate (product): recommendation: publish interim status update to status.redwood.ai and to affected customers. Frank to draft.

frank (cs): drafting now: "We are investigating elevated errors in ap-south-2 that may affect latency/availability. We have applied routing and internal mitigations; further updates in 30m."

lee (oncall): Ops checklist: set incident priority P1 due to customer impact threshold crossed (>=10% requests failing). Notify executives.

ops-bot: Incident priority set to P1. Paging execs: @cto @ops-lead.

nora (sre): current metrics (post-mitigations, +15m): Hosted API ap-south-2 5xx down to 7%, p95 latency down to 320ms. Dedicated pools improved to 5-8% 5xx. Still elevated but stabilizing.

samir (infra): note — CloudWatch Logs ingest is still throttled per shard. AWS suggests exponential backoff; we've implemented additional jitter and backoff in exporters. Also requested increase to PutLogEvents quota via support case.

lee (oncall): can we disable non-essential observability for all ap-south-2 hosts until CW recovers? We already did pool-a; propose disabling in pool-b as well. Need sign-off.

nora (sre): approve. Doing that now.

frank (cs): sent status update to top affected customers and posted to status page.

aws-support-bot: Update on Case 1234567890: AWS requested debug logs and will escalate to service team.

samir (infra): question for product: do any production features require CloudWatch logs for correctness? we risk losing traces for a short window.

kate (product): acceptable for now; prefer availability over logs. Keep events we need for replay.

lee (oncall): handoff plan: I'm handing to nora for detailed postmortem and remediation. I'll stay in channel for transparency. Handoff @ 2026-03-15T13:05Z.

nora (sre): taking over incident lead. Next steps: 1) coordinate with AWS for quota increase and root cause; 2) plan permanent mitigation (credential caching, reduced CW fanout, region fallback automation); 3) runbook updates. Will assemble timeline.

frank (cs): will follow-up with customers with detailed timeline when we have more.

lee (oncall): thanks team. Remaining ask: product to convene prioritized list for telemetry we can't disable.

kate (product): will compile and send to nora.

nora (sre): current status summary to include in incident record:
- Impact: elevated 5xx and latency for Hosted API and Dedicated pools in ap-south-2 (peak ~18% 5xx, now ~6-8%).
- Mitigations: routing override to ap-south-1, long-lived instance profile rollout, disabled non-critical CW exports, throttled background jobs, increased exporter backoff jitter.
- Customer impact: some requests failing; top customers notified; no data loss reported.
- Next: AWS case escalation, quota requests, runbook updates, automation for cross-region fallback.

ops-bot: Incident recorded: incident-2026-03-15-3123456789.

nora (sre): assigning follow-ups: samir -> implement permanent credential caching (RFC due 3/22), kate -> telemetry list (due 3/16), lee -> post-incident runbook edits (due 3/18).

frank (cs): closing initial customer notification thread. Will reopen for updates.

lee (oncall): closing active paging for this shift; nora remains lead. If errors spike above 12% revert routing.

nora (sre): will post final incident report after root cause confirmed. thanks all for quick response :party-parrot:
